description: Width tiers for Languages — Background Language Learner Pathway, Foundation band
subject: Languages — Background Language Learner

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest honest floor for the descriptor's command term at Foundation level. For communicating descriptors: the minimum range of contexts or interaction types in which students have used the target language. For understanding descriptors: the minimum range of language features or cultural connections noticed and described.
width_notes.typical_width: The full descriptor scope as ACARA elaborations indicate — the range of contexts, features or cultural connections a well-taught Foundation class would have engaged with.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions that add new contexts, language features or cultural connection types — not harder versions of the same. Appropriate for background language learners who bring rich prior home-language experience to school.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations for the Chinese Background Language Learner pathway (Foundation) used as source data. Elaborations are examples of how the descriptor might be addressed; they are not exhaustive or prescriptive. Chinese-specific references are preserved as representative examples of the generic target-language principle.

AC9LCHF01.minimum_width: Recognise and respond to at least three familiar classroom instructions or greetings in the target language through action, gesture or word; communicate at least one piece of personal information using a modelled phrase with support.
AC9LCHF01.typical_width: Recognise and respond to a range of familiar spoken expressions — greetings, classroom instructions, questions about self; use formulaic expressions appropriately in play-based and social contexts; communicate personal information and simple preferences using modelled sentences; participate in brief personal introduction exchanges with teacher and peers.
wider: Use target language in spontaneous play-based scenarios — shops, doctors, family role-play — adapting familiar phrases to new contexts
Share target language expressions with family or community members outside school, demonstrating use across social contexts beyond the classroom
Explore how greetings and communication conventions in the target language compare with those in English and other languages known in the class
elaborations: greeting each other and using appropriate terms of address, gestures, and body language, for example, [TL], [TL], [TL], [TL]
responding to classroom instructions and routines, for example, at the beginning of the class responding to, [TL],[TL],[TL]
sharing personal information about topics such as name, age and family
making simple requests using appropriate manners, for example, [TL]
using puppets to perform role-play exchanges about family
expressing thanks, apologies, likes and dislikes using formulaic expressions
using formulaic exclamations spontaneously when interacting with peers
identifying which languages they know and are learning
participating in songs, rhymes and chants with repetitive language and actions
participating in play-based experiences using props or costumes

AC9LCHF02.minimum_width: Notice and imitate at least two distinctive sounds or sound patterns in the target language; identify at least one feature of the target language writing system that is similar to or different from English.
AC9LCHF02.typical_width: Explore and notice the sound system of the target language — tones, rhythms, distinctive vowels and consonants; compare with English sound patterns; participate in songs and chants that highlight sound features; notice features of the target language writing system alongside English; compare word and sentence patterns across the two languages using teacher-supported metalanguage.
wider: Compare animal sounds, counting rhymes or familiar expressions across the target language and English — identify where sounds are shared, similar or distinctly different
Explore how the writing system of the target language reflects meaning — for example, how component elements contribute to character meaning
Investigate borrowed words or expressions that appear in both languages in written form — notice what stays the same and what changes
elaborations: listening to and performing nursery rhymes and stories with rhythms, tones and sound patterns
participating in tone-guessing activities to identify different tones
writing syllables in Pinyin with correct tone marks
singing a Pinyin alphabet song to understand romanisation of sounds
playing pair-matching card games matching tones and initials to finals
making and copying components, characters and/or words using varied materials
noticing similarities and differences between punctuation conventions in the target language and English
understanding basic rules of word order in the target language

AC9LCHF03.minimum_width: Identify at least one context (community, country, family setting, celebration) where the target language is used; identify at least one cultural practice associated with the target language and describe the language used in connection with it.
AC9LCHF03.typical_width: Explore the cultural contexts in which the target language is spoken; connect target language cultural practices — celebrations, stories, songs, games — to students' own experience; reflect on the role of the target language in own identity and daily life; explore how people belong to more than one language and cultural community.
wider: Compare a cultural practice from the target language community with a similar practice in another community represented in the class — identify similarities and differences in associated language
Explore how First Nations Australian languages are each connected to specific communities and places, comparing with how the target language is connected to cultural community and belonging
Create a personal artefact — a drawing, bilingual caption, or illustrated sentence — representing own language and cultural identity
elaborations: identifying countries and regions where the target language is used as a language of communication
exploring symbols and language used by First Nations Australians and in target language communities, identifying similarities and differences
discussing the role of the target language in their own lives — cultural events, food preferences, overseas travel
exploring cultural symbols and practices through stories, songs, dances, games and crafts
sharing information about their family — country of origin, languages spoken, locations of extended family
comparing classroom interactions with those in target language communities to identify similarities and differences
using gestures, words and phrases that reflect aspects of the target language culture
discussing meanings of colloquial phrases used on specific occasions, such as New Year wishes
